artifacts.synopsis: RE Tom Turner complained against South Florida Presbytery's action finding the Session of Cross Community Church guilty of important delinquencies related to alleged sexual abuse incidents involving the pastor's sons, without formal judicial process. The SJC denied the complaint as to Presbytery's right to investigate under BCO 40-4, but sustained it as to the finding of guilt and imposed censures, holding that formal judicial process (indictment, plea, and trial) under BCO 40-6 was required before findings of guilt could be entered, and remanded to Presbytery.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained the appeal of the Session of FPC North Port from the Presbytery of Southwest Florida's judgment suspending the Session, reversing the judgment in whole and dismissing all charges. The Commission held that Presbytery's citation and trial of the FPC Session for failure to initiate ecclesiastical process against a church member was constitutionally out of order, compounding the same errors identified in Case 2013-07, as Presbytery had failed to follow the required steps of BCO 40-5 before proceeding against the Session.

artifacts.title: the Session of Hope Community Church v. Central Carolina Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.

artifacts.title: William G. Mitchell v. The Presbytery of the Ascension
artifacts.synopsis: RE Mitchell appealed his indefinite suspension from office as Ruling Elder by the Presbytery of the Ascension, arising from allegations he broke a promise to take a sabbatical from Session and failed in his duties as Clerk of Session. The SJC vacated the judgment on Specification No. 2 (promise-breaking) and remanded for possible new trial, and reversed and dismissed Specification No. 6 (clerk duties) as insufficiently serious to warrant trial.

artifacts.title: PCA v. Korean Capital Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The 40th General Assembly had cited Korean Capital Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from October 6, 2008. The SJC noted that Korean Capital Presbytery submitted responses approved by the Presbytery under BCO 10-4, and found those responses acceptable.

artifacts.title: Presbyterian Church in America v. Warrior Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The 39th General Assembly had cited Warrior Presbytery for failure to respond to exceptions of substance in minutes from 2007 and 2009. The SJC reviewed Warrior Presbytery's responses submitted under BCO 10-4 and found them acceptable, resolving the citation.
